questions.question: A VIP receives TCP/443 on WAN, but the private server sees nothing and the intended policy counter stays at zero. What should be checked first?

options.text: The server listener and TLS certificate on the mapped port
options.feedback: Those matter after traffic reaches the server. A zero policy counter indicates the flow has not matched the expected forwarding policy yet.

options.text: The FortiGate DNS cache and resolver order for this hostname
options.feedback: DNS resolution is not the first boundary when the packet already targets the configured external VIP address.

options.text: The VIP interface binding and destination object in the policy
options.feedback: Correct. Confirm extintf matches ingress and the firewall policy destination references this VIP; then inspect service and source matching.

options.text: The FortiGate HA heartbeat priority and session pickup state
options.feedback: HA state can affect forwarding, but the first evidence is a zero policy hit on a specific VIP flow.

questions.question: Ping to the FortiGate WAN address stops after an unused VIP is created for that same address. ARP reply is enabled. Which behavior best explains this?

options.text: The VIP can claim the address and DNAT matching ICMP traffic
options.feedback: Correct. With ARP reply enabled, FortiGate treats the VIP as a local address; an unused VIP can affect routing and may forward traffic to its mapped address.

options.text: The VIP disables the WAN interface's ICMP responder globally
options.feedback: The VIP does not globally disable ICMP response. Its local-address and translation behavior is the relevant boundary.

options.text: The VIP forces replies for that address through the default route
options.feedback: The documented side effect is the opposite: the configured VIP may prevent routing-table forwarding for that address.

options.text: The VIP changes the upstream router's ARP cache aging timer
options.feedback: The FortiGate's ARP reply behavior changes ownership on the local segment; it does not set the upstream router's timer.

questions.question: A public service listens on TCP/8443 internally but must be reached as TCP/443 externally. Which VIP fields express that translation?

options.text: Set extip private and mappedip public for reverse DNAT
options.feedback: That reverses the address direction. The client targets extip; FortiGate translates it to mappedip.

options.text: Set HTTPS service and source NAT on the VIP object
options.feedback: Service matching belongs to the firewall policy. The VIP needs explicit port-forward mapping for this translation.

options.text: Set extport to 443 and mappedport to 8443
options.feedback: Those values reverse the required mapping. External 443 must map to internal 8443.

options.text: Enable port forwarding; map external 443 to internal 8443
options.feedback: Correct. Use the external port clients target and the mapped port the internal service actually listens on.

questions.question: Central NAT is enabled and an engineer cannot find the normal Virtual IPs page. Where should DNAT VIPs be managed?

options.text: Policy & Objects > IP Pools for source-NAT address objects
options.feedback: IP pools are used for source NAT address allocation, not the central DNAT object page.

options.text: Policy & Objects > DNAT & Virtual IPs
options.feedback: Correct. Fortinet documents that central NAT moves DNAT configuration to this page.

options.text: Network > Static Routes under the routing controls
options.feedback: Static routes determine next hops after policy processing; they do not define the VIP translation object.

options.text: Security Fabric > Fabric Connectors for device enrollment
options.feedback: Fabric connectors manage integrations such as logging and analytics, not the DNAT object store.

questions.question: Which observation most directly proves that a VIP translated the destination from the public endpoint to the private server?

options.text: Capture shows destination translation from WAN to server VLAN
options.feedback: Correct. Comparing both sides of the FortiGate demonstrates the actual DNAT result, while the policy counter confirms admission separately.

options.text: The VIP object appears in the saved configuration backup
options.feedback: Configuration presence proves intent, not that the live packet matched the object or was translated.

options.text: The server answers a ping from its own local VLAN
options.feedback: That proves local server reachability, not that inbound WAN traffic traversed the VIP and policy.

options.text: The WAN interface reports carrier, speed and full duplex
options.feedback: Physical link state does not establish VIP matching, DNAT translation or policy admission.

questions.question: One policy package must use logical interface VOICE, mapped to port3 on one FortiGate and a zone on another. Which feature fits?

options.text: A separate policy package for every model
options.feedback: Separate packages can work, but they duplicate policy logic and do not use FortiManager's normalized-interface abstraction.

options.text: A CLI template that renames the physical interfaces
options.feedback: Renaming interfaces changes the device configuration and is not the normalized-interface mapping mechanism.

options.text: A normalized interface with per-device and platform mappings
options.feedback: Correct. The policy references one logical name while FortiManager resolves the target interface or zone during installation.

options.text: An SD-WAN service rule with member priority
options.feedback: SD-WAN services select traffic paths on a FortiGate; they do not resolve FortiManager policy interface names.

questions.question: Creating a normalized interface with a physical per-platform interface name fails with 'dynamic-interface default mapping has been used'. What is the documented next step?

options.text: Delete the device default route and retry the normalized-interface install
options.feedback: Routing configuration is unrelated to the normalized-interface default mapping guard.

options.text: Remove the default per-platform mapping rule from the default normalized interface
options.feedback: Correct. FortiManager documents this prerequisite when a physical interface name is used in a per-platform mapping rule.

options.text: Convert the policy package to workflow mode, then approve it
options.feedback: Workflow mode controls change approvals; it does not resolve the normalized-interface default-map conflict.

options.text: Create a separate ADOM and re-import the managed devices
options.feedback: A new ADOM is unnecessary. Fix the specific default mapping rule in the existing ADOM.

questions.question: A CLI script modifies a policy object's dynamic_mapping data. Where should that script be run?

options.text: On the FortiGate local CLI after package installation completes
options.feedback: That bypasses FortiManager's policy database and can create configuration drift.

options.text: In the FortiManager Device Database for each managed target
options.feedback: The dynamic mapping belongs to the policy object; the guide distinguishes policy-package execution from Device Database execution.

options.text: On the FortiAnalyzer supervisor through its JSON API endpoint
options.feedback: FortiAnalyzer is not the policy-object execution target for FortiManager dynamic mappings.

options.text: Against the FortiManager policy package's dynamic-mapping data
options.feedback: Correct. The dynamic mapping CLI script must run on a policy package rather than the Device Database.

questions.question: A normalized interface has a correct platform mapping, but one FortiGate still installs the wrong zone. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: A per-device mapping overrides the platform default for that device
options.feedback: Correct. Inspect the device/VDOM-specific mapping before changing the platform-wide rule.

options.text: The ADOM database always prefers the first physical port
options.feedback: FortiManager does not use a universal first-port rule; it resolves configured mapping objects.

options.text: The FortiGate policy service rewrites interface names after install
options.feedback: Service objects do not rewrite interface names. The generated policy should reflect the mapping selected by FortiManager.

options.text: The firewall session table has cached an earlier zone
options.feedback: Session state cannot explain an incorrect interface name in the installed policy configuration.

questions.question: The FortiGate Logging & Analytics connector shows Unauthorized even though the FortiAnalyzer IP is reachable. What is the next correct action?

options.text: Rebuild the FortiAnalyzer ADOM database and restart Analytics services
options.feedback: ADOM and Analytics state are downstream of Fabric authorization; rebuilding them will not approve the FortiGate.

options.text: Enable all FortiGate traffic and event log categories
options.feedback: Log-type selection controls data upload after authorization. It does not complete the trust-enrollment step.

options.text: Verify Fabric Authorization address and port, then approve the device
options.feedback: Correct. Configure the endpoint on FortiAnalyzer, then use the FortiGate connector's Authorize flow and approve with administrator credentials.

options.text: Change the FortiGate interface MTU and restart its logging process
options.feedback: MTU may affect transport, but the explicit Unauthorized state points to the authorization transaction.

questions.question: A FortiGate is authorized in Device Manager but its logs are absent. Which boundary should be tested next?

options.text: Repeat the Fabric authorization approval for the same device
options.feedback: The device is already authorized. Repeating approval will not repair the separate log-transport or ingestion path.

options.text: Check log upload settings, OFTP reachability and ADOM log state
options.feedback: Correct. Authorization proves trust enrollment; log delivery, reception and Analytics indexing must be verified independently.

options.text: Review the FortiGate administrator password and account lockout policy
options.feedback: The administrator credential was sufficient to authorize the device; password complexity is not the log-ingestion path.

options.text: Refresh the Security Fabric topology display and connector status
options.feedback: Topology refresh affects display, not whether the device uploads and FortiAnalyzer indexes logs.

questions.question: What does a FortiGate appearing as an authorized device in FortiAnalyzer Device Manager prove?

options.text: All configured log types have been inserted into Analytics
options.feedback: Authorization does not prove log receipt or database insertion; inspect the log pipeline separately.

options.text: Every FortiGate policy is synchronized with the FortiAnalyzer device
options.feedback: FortiAnalyzer authorization is not policy-package installation or configuration synchronization.

options.text: The FortiGate has a working default route to the Internet
options.feedback: The authorization relationship proves neither general Internet routing nor application reachability.

options.text: The Fabric trust-enrollment step completed for this FortiGate
options.feedback: Correct. It establishes the authorized-device relationship, not the later log transport and query path.

questions.question: The authorization request never appears in FortiAnalyzer, while the FortiGate connector is enabled. Which check has the highest value?

options.text: Confirm FortiGate can reach the configured authorization address and port
options.feedback: Correct. A wrong endpoint or port can prevent the request from reaching the authorization service before administrator approval is possible.

options.text: Increase Analytics retention only after confirming logs are arriving
options.feedback: Retention controls stored data age, not the arrival of an authorization request.

options.text: Check Device Manager serial and ADOM assignment for duplicates
options.feedback: Datasets query logs and cannot authorize a device that has not completed the connector transaction.

options.text: Confirm connector identity and FortiGate serial number match
options.feedback: A hostname convention may help administration, but the authorization endpoint and connector path are the first boundary.

questions.question: A receiver sends IGMPv3 reports, but the FortiSwitch querier is configured for IGMPv2 and the group is not learned. What is the likely issue?

options.text: The multicast source must use a globally routable public IP
options.feedback: The source address class is not the key issue; the snooping process must understand the host's IGMP report version.

options.text: The IGMP version mismatch prevents receiver membership from being learned
options.feedback: Correct. Match the configured querier version to the host reports before changing VLAN membership or flood behavior.

options.text: The switch needs a static route to each multicast receiver
options.feedback: IGMP snooping is a Layer-2 membership-learning function and does not require a unicast static route per receiver.

options.text: The receiver must renew DHCP before joining the multicast group
options.feedback: DHCP state is separate from IGMP membership reporting; a DHCP renewal does not create the group entry.

questions.question: Unknown multicast flooding is disabled, no group entry exists, and no mRouter port is learned. What happens to an unregistered multicast stream?

options.text: It is flooded to all access ports by default
options.feedback: That describes the enabled flood-unknown-multicast behavior, not the documented default.

options.text: It is converted into broadcast traffic by the querier
options.feedback: The querier sends membership queries; it does not convert unknown multicast into broadcast.

options.text: It is not forwarded to ordinary listener ports
options.feedback: Correct. With unknown-multicast flooding disabled, unregistered multicast is forwarded only to mRouter ports; with none known, it can be discarded.

options.text: It is routed to the FortiGate management interface
options.feedback: The snooping decision is per VLAN and does not send unknown streams to a management interface by default.

questions.question: Why must the IGMP snooping aging-time be greater than the query-interval?

options.text: So a learned listener entry survives until its next query refresh
options.feedback: Correct. Membership state must remain alive long enough for the next expected query/report cycle.

options.text: To keep multicast packets below the TTL used by unicast
options.feedback: TTL is a packet forwarding field and is unrelated to the snooping table aging timer.

options.text: To force FortiGate to remain the only querier in the VLAN
options.feedback: The timer relationship does not elect a specific querier; it preserves membership between query cycles.

options.text: To limit unknown multicast flooding to the membership aging window
options.feedback: Unknown-multicast flooding is a separate forwarding policy and is not controlled by the age/query relationship.

questions.question: Which command provides direct evidence that the switch learned a multicast group and listener ports?

options.text: get switch trunk
options.feedback: This shows trunk state, not the per-VLAN IGMP membership table.

options.text: diagnose switch-controller switch-info
options.feedback: General switch-controller information does not replace the snooping group table.

options.text: show system interface
options.feedback: Interface configuration shows VLAN and addressing, not dynamically learned IGMP listeners.

options.text: get switch igmp-snooping group
options.feedback: Correct. The group table shows learned multicast membership and related port state; it does not prove the source is transmitting the expected group.

questions.question: A scanner has poor uplink throughput after airtime fairness is enabled. Which statement best explains why ATF may not help?

options.text: ATF is available only on 6 GHz radios
options.feedback: That is incorrect. Fortinet documents 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz support for this feature.

options.text: ATF schedules AP-to-client downlink data, not client-to-AP uplink
options.feedback: Correct. The AP controls downlink airtime; uplink-heavy traffic requires a different RF or traffic-control approach.

options.text: ATF requires WPA3 Enterprise security on the SSID
options.feedback: ATF is not tied to authentication type; the guide lists Open, PSK and Enterprise use cases.

options.text: ATF schedules beacon and management frames only
options.feedback: The feature applies to data and not control/management frames, so this reverses the documented scope.

questions.question: Two SSIDs have airtime weights 80 and 20. What should an engineer expect under comparable simultaneous downlink demand?

options.text: The first SSID receives four times the guaranteed Mbps rate
options.feedback: ATF allocates airtime share, not a fixed Mbps reservation; RF rates and retries affect throughput.

options.text: The first SSID can transmit only when the second is idle
options.feedback: The weights do not create strict time-exclusive scheduling; they establish relative airtime allocation under demand.

options.text: The first SSID receives roughly four times the scheduled data airtime
options.feedback: Correct. The 80/20 example is a relative airtime weight, not a byte-rate or per-client guarantee.

options.text: The second SSID is blocked whenever the first SSID has traffic
options.feedback: A 20-percent weight does not disable the lower-weight VAP; it still receives its configured share.

questions.question: Which AP-side command most directly shows configured and applied airtime fairness weights?

options.text: cw_diag -c atf
options.feedback: Correct. The output reports radio ATF state and configured/applied weights for each WLAN.

options.text: cw_diag -c station
options.feedback: Station diagnostics can show client state, but this is not the documented ATF weight verification command.

options.text: diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c vap
options.feedback: This can expose controller/VAP information, but the guide identifies cw_diag -c atf for ATF weights.

options.text: get wireless-controller status
options.feedback: General controller status does not directly show the applied per-VAP airtime weights.

questions.question: ATF is enabled on a radio, but the profile uses vap-all disable and omits the target SSID from the vaps list. What is the likely result?

options.text: The SSID inherits the default airtime weight configured for its radio
options.feedback: The default weight does not add an omitted VAP to a radio whose VAP list is explicitly restricted.

options.text: The AP moves the SSID to another available radio automatically
options.feedback: The profile does not promise automatic reassignment of an omitted VAP to another radio.

options.text: The controller disables client authentication for that SSID's VAP
options.feedback: VAP selection and ATF membership do not disable the SSID's authentication configuration.

options.text: That SSID is excluded from the radio's configured ATF VAP set
options.feedback: Correct. With vap-all disabled, the profile must explicitly include the VAPs to be scheduled by that radio.

questions.question: A guest sees the waiting page after requesting access, but the request expires before approval. What is the first timing check?

options.text: The guest template's account duration after successful registration
options.feedback: Account duration controls an approved account's lifetime, not the pending request timeout.

options.text: The portal's pending-request timeout, defaulting to 20 minutes
options.feedback: Correct. FortiNAC documents a default request expiry of 20 minutes when a sponsor/request pool does not respond.

options.text: The switch port's MAC authentication and aging timer
options.feedback: Switch MAC aging can affect endpoint location, but it does not control the FortiNAC portal request expiry.

options.text: The guest's DHCP lease timer on the isolated VLAN
options.feedback: DHCP lease timing is independent of the sponsor request state machine.

questions.question: A sponsor says no registration email arrived. Which prerequisite should be verified before changing VLAN enforcement?

options.text: The sponsor has the required admin role, profile and email
options.feedback: Correct. The sponsor needs a FortiNAC administrator identity/profile and email for the request notification path.

options.text: The guest endpoint has a static address on the isolated VLAN
options.feedback: A static address is not required for the sponsor email transaction and will not fix an invalid sponsor profile.

options.text: The guest template uses a non-expiring account duration setting
options.feedback: Account duration affects the created account after approval; it does not determine whether the sponsor receives the request.

options.text: The production VLAN has a configured DHCP relay helper
options.feedback: That is a downstream network service dependency, not a prerequisite for sponsor notification.

questions.question: The sponsor approves a guest request and credentials are delivered, but the endpoint remains isolated. Which boundary is next?

options.text: Recreate the sponsor administrator and reassign the approval profile
options.feedback: The sponsor already approved the request; account recreation is not the first post-approval check.

options.text: Rotate the LDAP bind password and retest directory authentication
options.feedback: The guest account may be locally created from a template; a directory bind change does not explain a post-login release failure.

options.text: Verify guest account creation, login and switch/AP reconfiguration
options.feedback: Correct. Approval, account creation, credential delivery, login and network release are distinct transitions.

options.text: Increase the pending-request timeout before another approval attempt
options.feedback: The request is already approved; changing the pending timeout does not repair the network release path.

questions.question: Where is the expiry duration for a self-registered guest account defined?

options.text: In the sponsor administrator's email profile
options.feedback: Email profile controls notification delivery, not the guest account lifetime.

options.text: In the switch port's authentication timer
options.feedback: Port authentication timers can trigger reauthentication but do not define the guest account expiry date.

options.text: In the captive portal's pending-request timeout
options.feedback: That timeout expires an unanswered request; it is not the account duration after approval.

options.text: In the self-registered guest template's Account Duration
options.feedback: Correct. The template's account duration determines when the created guest account expires.

questions.question: The LDAP connection test succeeds, but Add New does not display 'Loaded from Directory' for a user. What should be checked next?

options.text: Import the user's LDAP group before creating the local account
options.feedback: The recent FortiNAC-F tip states that group import is not required merely to read the user; the user DN must be readable.

options.text: Change the host's access VLAN to the production network
options.feedback: VLAN placement is downstream of identity lookup and cannot make an LDAP user DN readable.

options.text: Check user ID and LDAP read permission on the DN
options.feedback: Correct. A successful bind does not prove the service account can read the specific user DN or that the entered ID matches.

options.text: Disable scheduled directory synchronization for this user account
options.feedback: Synchronization is not the first boundary for an Add New lookup that fails to populate directory fields.

questions.question: A user record shows 'Loaded from Directory' and has a role, but the endpoint policy still sees an unknown user. What is the most likely missing relationship?

options.text: The imported user is not linked to the correct host record
options.feedback: Correct. FortiNAC separates user and host objects; the host must be edited and the user explicitly associated.

options.text: The LDAP server is not acting as the DHCP relay service
options.feedback: LDAP supplies identity data; DHCP relay is not the relationship between a user and a FortiNAC host.

options.text: The user's directory group was not imported into FortiGate
options.feedback: The tip notes group import is unnecessary for the user lookup; the missing link is usually the host association.

options.text: The FortiNAC-F switch profile is missing an IGMP querier
options.feedback: IGMP snooping has no role in user-to-host identity association.

questions.question: Is importing the entire LDAP group hierarchy required to manually read one user's directory record?

options.text: Yes; FortiNAC requires a complete group import before user lookup
options.feedback: The Community procedure explicitly says the group does not need to be imported just to read the user.

options.text: No; FortiNAC must be able to read the user's DN
options.feedback: Correct. The LDAP connection must exist and the user DN must be readable; group import is not the prerequisite for this task.

options.text: Only when the endpoint uses a static IPv4 address
options.feedback: IP addressing does not determine whether a user DN can be read from LDAP.

options.text: Only when the user is assigned an administrator profile
options.feedback: The procedure assigns a FortiNAC role after the user is loaded; it does not require an administrator profile for every user.

questions.question: A manually created user ID matches a directory user ID. What can a later directory synchronization do?

options.text: Delete the matching host and all network adapters
options.feedback: The documentation does not say a matching user ID deletes host adapters as part of ordinary synchronization.

options.text: Convert the directory user into a local-only identity
options.feedback: A matching ID preserves the directory relationship; it does not automatically convert the user to local-only authentication.

options.text: Remove the user role and clear all group membership
options.feedback: The documented behavior is directory data refresh, not automatic removal of role and group assignments.

options.text: Overwrite directory-owned user fields with the directory values
options.feedback: Correct. FortiNAC matches by User ID and refreshes fields such as name and email from the directory; manual edits to those fields can be overwritten.

questions.question: On a FortiAuthenticator build before 8.0.4, an EAP-TTLS client has no separate OTP prompt and the RADIUS log reports a missing token. What legacy workaround is documented?

options.text: Enter the LDAP password immediately followed by the current OTP
options.feedback: Correct for the documented pre-8.0.4 behavior. The inner credential is submitted in one field because challenge-based EAP-TTLS 2FA is not supported in that release family.

options.text: Send the OTP as a second RADIUS username attribute
options.feedback: The documented workaround is password-plus-OTP concatenation in the password field, not a second username attribute.

options.text: Disable the EAP-TTLS TLS tunnel and send PAP in clear text
options.feedback: The TLS tunnel protects the inner authentication. Disabling it would weaken security and does not implement the supported workaround.

options.text: Move the FortiToken assignment to the FortiGate user object
options.feedback: The token is assigned and validated by FortiAuthenticator in this design; moving it to FortiGate does not fix the missing EAP-TTLS challenge.

questions.question: A FortiAuthenticator 8.0.4 deployment is being migrated from the older EAP-TTLS concatenation workaround. What should the engineer do?

options.text: Keep concatenation because EAP-TTLS still lacks OTP challenges
options.feedback: That describes the older documentation boundary, but Fortinet's October 2026 update states support is available from 8.0.4.

options.text: Move every user to EAP-MSCHAPv2 without testing client support
options.feedback: Changing EAP methods alters the authentication protocol and client compatibility; it is not the documented 8.0.4 EAP-TTLS update.

options.text: Use 8.0.4 challenge-based EAP-TTLS and verify policy support
options.feedback: Correct. The version update says not to use the legacy concatenation workaround on 8.0.4; validate the new policy flow and supported client versions.

options.text: Remove the FortiAuthenticator EAP server certificate from policy
options.feedback: The TLS server certificate remains part of EAP-TTLS; removing it would break server authentication rather than enable OTP challenge behavior.

questions.question: FortiAuthenticator is configured as a RADIUS proxy to a remote server. Which statement about its local EAP settings is correct?

options.text: Local EAP settings always override the remote server's EAP policy
options.feedback: The documentation says local EAP settings apply to sessions terminated by FortiAuthenticator, not sessions proxied to a remote RADIUS server.

options.text: Local EAP settings apply only when FortiAuthenticator terminates the EAP session
options.feedback: Correct. If EAP is proxied, troubleshoot the remote RADIUS server's EAP configuration and trust path.

options.text: Local EAP settings are used only for MAC authentication bypass
options.feedback: MAB is a separate authentication type; EAP termination/proxy behavior determines which EAP settings apply.

options.text: Local EAP settings are selected by the FortiGate firewall policy ID
options.feedback: The RADIUS client and matching policy determine the authentication flow; the firewall policy ID does not select FAC EAP termination.

questions.question: LDAP authentication succeeds in a standalone test, but IKEv2 EAP-TTLS still fails. Which evidence is most useful next?

options.text: The workstation's DHCP lease and local DNS resolver settings
options.feedback: A lease proves network addressing, not the EAP inner method or second-factor transaction.

options.text: The FortiGate SD-WAN rule order for the VPN destination
options.feedback: SD-WAN path selection may affect reachability, but it does not prove the RADIUS policy and EAP exchange completed.

options.text: The FortiAuthenticator DNS cache and LDAP lookup timeout
options.feedback: DNS may affect server reachability, but the direct LDAP test already narrows the next investigation to the RADIUS/EAP flow.

options.text: Correlate EAP method, RADIUS policy, realm and token result
options.feedback: Correct. A direct LDAP test does not prove that the supplicant used the expected inner method or submitted the second factor.

questions.question: An SSH-key secret must use certificate-based authentication rather than a raw public key. Which secret field choice is required?

options.text: Select Public key with certificate in the SSH-key secret template
options.feedback: Correct. FortiPAM documents this option for FortiProduct (SSH Key) and Unix Account (SSH Key) templates.

options.text: Use a standard public key and attach a certificate file
options.feedback: A standard public key does not select the certificate-based SSH mode; use the dedicated Public key with certificate option.

options.text: Choose a Certificate template without storing SSH private-key material
options.feedback: The Certificate template stores a certificate artifact; it is not the SSH-key template's public-key authentication selector.

options.text: Use an associated secret with a password-only SSH credential
options.feedback: Associated secrets can supply launch credentials, but they do not change the SSH key's certificate authentication type.

questions.question: FortiPAM shows a valid SSH certificate in Secret Details, but the target rejects the launch. What does the display fail to prove?

options.text: That FortiPAM stored a credential for the configured SSH account
options.feedback: The validity display proves that certificate metadata is present in the secret; the question is about target-side acceptance.

options.text: That the certificate contains a current validity period for login
options.feedback: The validity period is displayed, so expiry metadata is visible. The remaining issue is the target's trust and principal policy.

options.text: That the target trusts the CA and accepts the certificate principal
options.feedback: Correct. FortiPAM's certificate status does not prove the target's trusted-CA configuration or authorized principal mapping.

options.text: That the secret can be opened in the FortiPAM UI
options.feedback: The UI display proves the object can be viewed; it does not establish the target SSH server's trust decision.

questions.question: Where are email notifications for expiring SSH certificates configured?

options.text: In the secret's launcher command and connection settings
options.feedback: Launcher settings control how the target session starts, not certificate expiry notifications.

options.text: In the Certificate tab of Email Alert Settings
options.feedback: Correct. FortiPAM documents certificate expiry notifications in the Certificate tab of Email Alert Settings.

options.text: In FortiPAM's HA heartbeat and failover configuration
options.feedback: HA heartbeat monitors appliance availability and is unrelated to certificate expiry email alerts.

options.text: In the target Unix account's password and login policy
options.feedback: Password policy controls password generation/rotation; it does not configure certificate email notifications.

questions.question: Which distinction matters when storing an SSH certificate in FortiPAM?

options.text: Both secret types store identical key material; only the label differs
options.feedback: The templates have different semantics and fields; they should not be treated as interchangeable.

options.text: The Certificate template is required for all SSH key secrets
options.feedback: The SSH-key template has its own Public key with certificate option; the generic Certificate template stores a certificate artifact.

options.text: The SSH-key template hides certificate validity from Secret Details
options.feedback: FortiPAM documents certificate details and validity status for SSH-key secrets using the certificate public-key option.

options.text: SSH-key stores a login key; Certificate stores a certificate file
options.feedback: Correct. Keep the SSH credential mode separate from a general certificate-file secret that may include private-key/passphrase fields.

questions.question: LDAPS authentication fails only when Check Certificate is enabled. The LDAP server certificate is issued to ldap01.example.com, but the profile uses 10.20.30.40. What is the likely cause?

options.text: FortiSIEM requires LDAP servers to listen on TCP port 1812
options.feedback: TCP/1812 is commonly associated with RADIUS, not the LDAP certificate name check.

options.text: The Base DN must include the LDAP server's certificate hostname
options.feedback: Base DN identifies directory search scope; it does not resolve the TLS certificate identity mismatch.

options.text: The profile hostname does not match the certificate CN/SAN
options.feedback: Correct. FortiSIEM checks the certificate CN or SAN against the LDAP host/IP entered in the profile.

options.text: The user must be a System Admin before LDAP can bind
options.feedback: Role assignment affects FortiSIEM authorization after authentication, not the TLS name check against the LDAP server.

questions.question: A SAML IdP authenticates a user, but FortiSIEM grants the wrong tenant role. What should be inspected?

options.text: Exact user match and SAML organization/role mappings to FortiSIEM values
options.feedback: Correct. FortiSIEM requires exact case-sensitive user matching and explicit mapping of IdP organization/role to FortiSIEM scope.

options.text: The Collector's syslog listener and event forwarding configuration
options.feedback: Collector event ingestion does not determine the user's SAML role or organization mapping.

options.text: The event worker's ClickHouse shard and storage placement
options.feedback: Event storage placement is unrelated to SAML user authorization.

options.text: The Supervisor's log retention and tenant partition settings
options.feedback: Retention controls stored event history, not the identity provider's role and tenant mapping.

questions.question: The external authentication profile's Test function succeeds, but the user still sees the wrong FortiSIEM pages. Which check is next?

options.text: Increase the provider's LDAP timeout and connection retry interval
options.feedback: The Test already succeeds; the issue may be user binding or authorization rather than provider reachability.

options.text: Bind the CMDB user to the profile, role and organization
options.feedback: Correct. Profile connectivity does not prove the local user object maps to the correct role and tenant.

options.text: Rebuild the FortiSIEM event database and query cache
options.feedback: The event database does not assign user roles or organization scope.

options.text: Change the username to include the domain suffix twice
options.feedback: Credential formatting may affect authentication, but the successful test and wrong page visibility point to authorization mapping.

questions.question: A user has two external authentication profiles. The first server is contacted successfully but rejects the credentials. What happens?

options.text: FortiSIEM continues to the next profile as a credential fallback
options.feedback: The documented behavior does not treat an authentication rejection as a simple fallback to another profile.

options.text: FortiSIEM disables the local user until an administrator resets it
options.feedback: The profile sequence does not imply an automatic local account disable action.

options.text: FortiSIEM chooses the profile with the newest trusted certificate on record
options.feedback: Profile selection follows the configured sequence and connection/authentication result, not certificate age.

options.text: The authentication process ends after the contacted server rejects the user
options.feedback: Correct. Multiple profiles are contacted sequentially until a connection succeeds; once a server is contacted and authentication fails, the process ends.

questions.question: A threat feed exists in FortiManager but does not appear in FortiSASE after synchronization. What is the first configuration check?

options.text: Check whether the feed URL uses a public address
options.feedback: Reachability may matter after the feed is synchronized, but the documented sync prerequisite is profile association.

options.text: Confirm every FortiGate in the ADOM is authorized in FortiAnalyzer
options.feedback: FortiAnalyzer authorization is unrelated to FortiManager-to-FortiSASE feed synchronization.

options.text: Confirm a Web Filter or DNS Filter profile references the feed
options.feedback: Correct. Only external feeds associated with Web Filter or DNS Filter profiles are synchronized.

options.text: Check whether the feed URL is present in a static route
options.feedback: A static route does not bind the threat feed to a supported filter profile.

questions.question: An external feed requires HTTP Basic Authentication. FortiManager sync succeeds, but FortiSASE cannot download entries. What is the missing step?

options.text: Recreate the FortiManager ADOM with a new name
options.feedback: ADOM naming does not transfer the Basic Authentication credentials.

options.text: Enter the feed username and password directly in FortiSASE
options.feedback: Correct. Fortinet documents that Basic Authentication credentials configured in FortiManager are not synchronized.

options.text: Add the feed URL to the FortiGate DNS database
options.feedback: DNS resolution does not supply the HTTP authentication credentials required by the feed server.

options.text: Disable SSL inspection for every SASE policy
options.feedback: SSL inspection is not the documented missing credential step and broad disabling would be an unsafe workaround.

questions.question: A feed card is visible in FortiSASE and contains the expected domains, but a test URL is allowed. What should be checked next?

options.text: The remote category action, profile group and traffic policy binding
options.feedback: Correct. Feed entries are data; enforcement requires the correct Web/DNS profile action and a policy that uses the profile.

options.text: The FortiManager administrator's password expiry and account status
options.feedback: The feed has already synchronized and contains entries; the remaining issue is likely profile/action binding.

options.text: The user's wireless airtime weight and SSID assignment
options.feedback: Wireless scheduling has no role in a FortiSASE Web/DNS category decision.

options.text: The FortiGate VIP ARP reply and external interface mapping
options.feedback: VIP ARP ownership is unrelated to SASE filter category enforcement.

questions.question: Which feed-count statement matches the FortiSASE 26.1.107 documentation?

options.text: A maximum of 21 external-host feeds, with no domain feeds
options.feedback: The documented 21 limit applies to DNS Filter Domains and Web Filter FQDNs; external-host feeds are excluded.

options.text: A maximum of 20 feeds across all feed types
options.feedback: That is not the stated limit for the DNS-domain/Web-FQDN synchronization workflow in this guide.

options.text: An unlimited number of feeds if FortiManager is the controller
options.feedback: FortiManager central management does not remove the documented category ID limit.

options.text: Up to 21 DNS-domain and Web-FQDN feeds; external-host feeds are excluded
options.feedback: Correct. The guide identifies category IDs 201–221 inclusive for the 21-feed limit and excludes external-host feeds from the count.

questions.question: Four IPsec overlays share two physical WAN links. The service uses bibandwidth but still evaluates each overlay independently. What setting changes the bandwidth reference to the shared physical link?

options.text: Set mode to manual and remove the health check
options.feedback: That changes service eligibility logic and removes SLA input; it does not select underlay bandwidth.

options.text: Set bandwidth-type underlay in the SD-WAN service
options.feedback: Correct. The default is overlay; underlay mode makes the load-balance service use shared physical underlay bandwidth.

options.text: Enable packet duplication on every overlay member
options.feedback: Duplication sends copies of traffic; it is not the bandwidth accounting selector.

options.text: Set the health-check server to the ISP gateway
options.feedback: The probe target affects health measurement, not whether the load-balance hash uses overlay or underlay capacity.

questions.question: Which hash mode uses the member's available bandwidth in both incoming and outgoing directions?

options.text: source-ip-based
options.feedback: Source-IP hashing pins traffic from a source to a member; it does not compare bidirectional available bandwidth.

options.text: outbandwidth
options.feedback: Outbandwidth selects using available outgoing bandwidth only.

options.text: bibandwidth
options.feedback: Correct. Bibandwidth evaluates available bandwidth for both incoming and outgoing traffic.

options.text: round-robin
options.feedback: Round-robin distributes traffic in circular order and does not use available bandwidth as its hash metric.

questions.question: A service has load-balance enabled and hash-mode bibandwidth, but the members still show overlay capacity. Which setting is missing?

options.text: set bandwidth-type underlay
options.feedback: Correct. The default bandwidth-type is overlay; explicitly set underlay to use shared physical capacity.

options.text: set update-static-route enable
options.feedback: Static-route update controls route installation based on health-check state, not bandwidth accounting type.

options.text: set priority-members all
options.feedback: The priority list determines eligible members; it does not change overlay versus underlay bandwidth measurement.

options.text: set mode manual
options.feedback: Manual mode changes SLA selection behavior and is not the underlay bandwidth selector.

questions.question: After setting bandwidth-type underlay, which command provides the documented service/member evidence?

options.text: diagnose sys sdwan health-check
options.feedback: Health-check output helps establish SLA state but does not show the selected service's bandwidth hash/member result.

options.text: get router info routing-table all
options.feedback: The routing table shows route selection, not the service's bandwidth-type and per-member bibandwidth evidence.

options.text: diagnose firewall iprope list
options.feedback: Policy lookup output is not the documented SD-WAN service bandwidth inspection.

options.text: diagnose sys sdwan service4
options.feedback: Correct. The example uses this command to inspect service mode, member bandwidth values and selected members.

questions.question: Two overlay members share the same best underlay bandwidth value and both appear selected. What should the engineer infer?

options.text: FortiGate is splitting every packet across both tunnels
options.feedback: The output does not establish per-packet striping; load balancing selects eligible members for session distribution.

options.text: Both members are eligible; tie-break/configuration order can determine preference
options.feedback: Correct. The example notes configuration-order tie-break behavior when values are equal; inspect sessions and service selection rather than assuming packet striping.

options.text: The SLA health check has been disabled automatically
options.feedback: Equal bandwidth values do not indicate that the health check is disabled.

options.text: Underlay bandwidth mode is not active on either member
options.feedback: Both selected members can still reflect underlay bandwidth; equal values alone do not mean the setting failed.
